faqs.q: How long does a central heating installation take?
faqs.a: A full central heating installation in a 3-bedroom semi-detached property typically takes 3-5 days. Larger properties or complex layouts take longer.

faqs.q: How many radiators do I need?
faqs.a: A qualified heating engineer calculates the heat loss for each room based on size, insulation, window area, and orientation, then sizes radiators accordingly. Undersized radiators are the most common reason homes never get warm enough.

faqs.q: What is a power flush and do I need one?
faqs.a: A power flush forces water and chemicals through your heating system at high velocity to remove sludge and corrosion debris. It's recommended before fitting a new boiler to an old system — debris from old pipes can damage a new boiler within months.

faqs.q: Should I add inhibitor to my heating system?
faqs.a: Yes — inhibitor prevents internal corrosion and sludge buildup, extending the life of your boiler and pump significantly. It should be added to all new installations and refreshed every 2-3 years.

localParagraph: Borthwick Hall, nestled in the rural landscape of Midlothian, Scotland, presents a distinctive set of considerations for central heating systems. The area features a mix of housing spanning multiple eras, from older stone-built properties characteristic of the Scottish countryside to more modern residential developments, each carrying its own heating requirements and pipe configurations. Water hardness in the region is mixed, which means homeowners should be mindful of scale accumulation within boilers and heat exchangers over time — a factor that can gradually reduce efficiency and shorten system lifespan if left unaddressed. Properties in Borthwick Hall that rely on oil-fired boilers, common in areas without mains gas infrastructure, may require particular attention to fuel line maintenance and annual servicing to ensure reliable performance through Scotland's often harsh winters. Whether you're managing a period property with older radiators and pipework or a newer build with underfloor heating, understanding how local water quality interacts with your system is essential for long-term reliability and cost-effective operation throughout the year.
whatItInvolves: Central heating installation or replacement involves fitting a new boiler, radiators, pipework, and controls to heat your home efficiently. A full system installation is a major project typically taking 3-5 days. A system upgrade — replacing radiators and adding smart controls to an existing boiler — takes 1-2 days. Both must be carried out by a Gas Safe registered engineer.
process: Survey: calculate heat loss per room and size radiators accordingly. First fix: run new pipework routes, fit radiator brackets, position boiler location. Second fix: hang radiators, connect boiler, fit programmer and thermostatic radiator valves. Commission: fill system, add inhibitor, balance radiators for even heat distribution, test all controls. Register with Building Control. Full system flush prior to filling removes debris that causes cold spots and pump failure.
whatToExpect: A full central heating installation in a 3-bed semi takes 3-5 days. You'll be without heating and hot water during the works — plan around this in winter. Modern systems with smart thermostats (Nest, Hive, Tado) can reduce heating bills by 20-30% through accurate scheduling. Your installer should provide a full commission certificate and Building Regulations notification.
intro: Central heating installation is one of the most significant investments a UK homeowner can make, directly affecting comfort, energy costs, and property value. Whether you are replacing an ageing system, converting from electric storage heaters to gas central heating, or installing heating in a new extension, the project involves careful planning of your boiler, radiators, pipework, controls, and insulation. A well-designed central heating system should last 15-20 years and can reduce annual energy bills by 20-40% compared to older or electric systems. The UK government's push toward net zero means heating technology is evolving rapidly, with heat pumps, hydrogen-ready boilers, and smart controls all becoming mainstream options alongside traditional gas systems.
serviceDetail: Central heating installation begins with a detailed heat loss calculation for your property. Your engineer will assess the size of each room, insulation levels, window types, and the building's thermal envelope to determine the correct boiler output and radiator sizes. This step is critical — an undersized system will not heat the house properly, while an oversized system wastes energy and money. The installation itself involves fitting the boiler (or heat pump), running copper or plastic pipework through the property to connect radiators in each room, installing a programmer and room thermostat (or smart controls), fitting a hot water cylinder if using a system or regular boiler, and connecting everything to the gas supply and flue. Expect significant disruption for 3-5 days — floors may need lifting for pipework, walls will need drilling for pipe runs and radiator brackets, and the system must be flushed, filled, and pressure-tested before commissioning.
pricing: A full central heating installation in the UK costs between £3,000 and £7,000 for a typical 3-bedroom house. This includes the boiler (£1,500-£3,000 for a quality combi or system boiler), radiators (£80-£200 each, typically 8-12 needed), pipework, controls, and labour. Converting from electric storage heaters to gas central heating is more expensive (£4,000-£8,000) due to the need for a new gas supply connection. Heat pump installations are significantly more costly at £8,000-£15,000 before government grants (the Boiler Upgrade Scheme currently offers £7,500 toward air source heat pumps). Labour typically accounts for 40-60% of the total cost and varies by region. Northern England and Scotland tend to be 15-25% cheaper than London and the South East for equivalent work.
whyLocal: Central heating installation requires multiple site visits — survey, installation (3-5 days), commissioning, and often a follow-up check. A local installer minimises travel time and cost on every visit, keeping the project on schedule and on budget. Local heating engineers also understand your area's specific characteristics — whether that means knowing that properties on your street have narrow pipe runs through solid Victorian walls, that your postcode is in a hard water area requiring a scale reducer, or that your neighbourhood is in a conservation area with specific flue positioning requirements. After installation, ongoing servicing and any warranty work is far easier with a local company who can attend within hours rather than days.
